rationale: Verified against SGCT Deut 28 (68 vv) and Deut 29 (29 vv) vs ME Deut 28 (69 vv) and Deut 29 (28 vv): the -1 offset is an intentional Saints.Bible parallel-reader versification mapping (placing SGCT 29:1 at 28:69 and SGCT 29:2-29 at 29:1-28), already documented at 28:69. Added a Rule 2 orientation note at Deut 29:1 so readers opening Chapter 29 immediately see the -1 Greek mapping without needing to read Chapter 28. Full 70-book / 1,291-chapter offset scan confirmed zero undetected offsets elsewhere.

Confirmed adopted SGCT Ps 6:1 reads ψαλμὸς τῷ Δαυίδ (multi-valent dative: "for / of / by / pertaining to David"). Under Rule 1 & Rule 5, retained the edition-wide literal dative "for David" pending human editor policy decision (GRC-HQ-015), and appended a neutral Rule 4 alternate-reading footnote on Ps 6:1 (and opening Psalter anchors Ps 3:1, 41:1, 49:1) documenting authorship and relational senses.

Confirmed adopted SGCT reads ἀνανεοῦσθαι δὲ τῷ πνεύματι τοῦ νοὸς ὑμῶν (bare articular dative τῷ πνεύματι without preposition) and no footnote existed on Eph 4:23. Retained "in the spirit of your mind" under Rule 1/Rule 5 and added a strictly neutral Rule 4 footnote documenting both the sphere/human-spirit reading ("in the spirit") and the instrumental/Holy-Spirit reading ("by the Spirit").

Confirmed genuine idiomatic mistranslation: adopted SGCT reads ἐπὶ χεῖρας Δαυὶδ ("upon the hands of David," calquing Hebrew al-yede = "according to the directions/order of"), not διὰ χειρῶν ("by the hands of"). Replaced "by the hands of David king of Israel" with "according to the directions of David king of Israel" and expanded the 3:10 footnote to preserve literal Greek epi cheiras Dauid.

Confirmed adopted SGCT Ps 61:1 reads ὑπὲρ Ἰδιθούν· ψαλμὸς τῷ Δαυίδ (two distinct constructions: ὑπέρ + genitive vs. dative τῷ). Fixed the double-"for" collision by rendering ὑπὲρ Ἰδιθούν as "on behalf of Jeduthun" (matching Ps 76:1 verbatim), retained "a psalm for David" pending GRC-HQ-015, and added a neutral Rule 4 footnote explaining both ὑπέρ and the multi-valent dative.
